title: My Weirdly Good Experience with Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm
body:
Okay so my skin is a whole thing. It’s like, dry but also gets weird bumps. Not acne. Just bumps. And it’s flaky but also shiny sometimes? I don’t get it. I’ve tried everything. The expensive stuff in the blue bottle from the mall. The drugstore lotion that smells like flowers and chemicals. The “clean” brand that cost like eighty dollars and did absolutely nothing. My bathroom cabinet is a graveyard of half-used bottles. My hands would get so dry in winter they’d crack by my knuckles. It hurt to make a fist. It was embarrassing. I’d be at work trying to type and just see these little red lines. So I was scrolling on my phone one night, it was like 11:47pm, and I saw this thing about tallow balm. Beef fat. For your face. I was eating pretzels and I just stopped chewing. Seriously? That’s a thing people do? But the person talking about it seemed normal. Not like a weirdo. And they mentioned this Bourbon Vanilla one. I was skeptical. Obviously. But my skin was so over everything else. I figured, how much worse could it get.

Anyway, I ordered the whipped tallow balm. From this little Etsy shop. It got here faster than I thought. It was a Tuesday maybe. The jar was small. Cute, though. Simple.

## How Beef Tallow for Skin Even Works

So I opened it. First thought: it doesn’t smell like beef. Thank god. It smelled like… vanilla. But not like cake. More like the vanilla bean thing my mom used to have in the sugar jar. Warm. Cozy. Like a bakery at 6am. The texture was weird. Not bad weird. It’s solid but soft. You scoop a little with your finger and it melts immediately. Like, the heat from your skin just turns it into oil. Which makes sense, I guess, because I read later that beef tallow is supposed to be really similar to the oils our skin already makes. Sebum. That’s the word. So it’s like giving your skin back what it knows how to use. Not some alien chemical from a lab. This one’s made from grass-fed cows, whipped up in France. Fancy. I felt fancy putting beef fat on my face. That’s a sentence I never thought I’d type.

My routine was a mess before. Serums, toners, creams. Layers. It took ten minutes. Now? I wash my face with water in the shower. Pat it kinda dry. Then I take a tiny bit of this tallow balm, rub it between my palms, and just press it onto my face. And my neck. And my hands. I use it everywhere. The dry patches on my elbows. My lips. Everywhere. It absorbs. Like, really absorbs. It doesn’t sit on top of your skin feeling greasy. You don’t look shiny. You just feel… normal. But hydrated. I don’t know how else to say it.

## What This Stuff Actually Did for My Skin

The first week I didn’t notice much. My skin felt softer maybe. But then, I was getting ready for work and I looked in the mirror. And the flaky skin around my nose was just… gone. The little dry bumps on my forehead were smoother. Not gone, but less angry. My hands. This is the big one. The cracks by my knuckles started to heal. They didn’t sting when I washed them. I could make a fist without that tight, painful feeling. It was wild. I kept looking at my hands like, are these mine?

After a few weeks, it was more obvious. My skin just felt more even. Calmer. When I’d put on makeup, it didn’t cling to dry spots. It just went on smooth. I didn’t have to pile on moisturizer before bed. I’d just use a dab of this tallow balm. My skin felt protected. Like it had a good barrier again. I have this one patch on my shin that gets super dry and itchy, always has, and I started putting the balm on it after I shaved. Game changer. No more itching. No more redness. It’s just… normal skin now. I sound like an infomercial but I’m not. I’m just sitting here with one sock on because I lost the other one. This is real.

I told my mom about it. She has psoriasis on her elbows. Really bad. She was using this prescription cream that cost a fortune. I gave her my jar to try for a week. She called me and was like, “What is in this? The itching stopped.” She ordered her own. Now we both use beef tallow. What a world.

## Would I Buy This Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did. I’m on my second jar of the Bourbon Vanilla tallow balm. The first one lasted me like, three months? And I used it every single day, all over. That’s pretty good. It’s spring now, but my skin doesn’t know that. It still gets dry from the wind. I keep the jar on my nightstand. It’s my go-to. For everything. Paper cut? Tallow. Windburn? Tallow. Dry lips? Tallow. It’s like the duct tape of skincare. I don’t know why it works. I just know that it does. And it smells nice. It’s a comforting smell. Not perfume-y. Just simple. It doesn’t fight with my coffee in the morning.

Look, if you’ve tried a million lotions and creams and your skin is still being difficult—dry, flaky, cracked, just generally pissed off—this might be worth a shot. This specific tallow balm. The whipped one with bourbon vanilla. It’s not magic. It’s just… really good at its job. It’s the best tallow for dry, angry skin I’ve found because it just sinks in and fixes the problem without a big fuss. It’s a natural moisturizer that actually moisturizes. My skin hasn’t felt this normal since I was a kid. I don’t have a better way to explain it.

So yeah. If you’re curious, I got mine from that Etsy shop. It’s just a small jar of whipped beef fat that made my skin stop hurting. My elbows are smooth. My hands don’t crack. I’m happy.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, it sounds nuts, but it actually is. Our skin produces oil called sebum to protect itself. Tallow is really similar to that. So it’s like giving your skin something it already knows how to use, not some weird synthetic thing. It absorbs deep. It doesn’t just sit on top.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about this too. But no, not for me. And I’m prone to little bumps. Because it’s so similar to our own skin oils, it absorbs properly. It doesn’t just block everything up. It’s the opposite—it helps your skin barrier get strong so it can do its job.

**What does Bourbon Vanilla tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like real vanilla. Not fake cake vanilla. More warm and cozy. Like a vanilla bean pod. It’s not sweet. It’s just… nice. It doesn’t smell like beef at all. Promise. It’s a stress-reducing smell, honestly. Very calming.
